item.subject: science
item.chapter_label: The night sky: Moon and calendars
item.stem:
Indira's family follows a purely lunar calendar. Each month begins with a new Moon, and twelve lunar months make one lunar year of about 354 days. A festival fixed to one lunar month falls in cool weather one year but, after several years, falls in hot weather.

Why does a purely lunar calendar not keep the same months aligned with the same seasons year after year?

options.A: The Moon's phases change randomly, so no lunar calendar can repeat in a regular way.
options.B: Twelve lunar months total about 354 days, which is shorter than the roughly 365-day seasonal year, so the lunar year ends earlier and the months drift through the seasons.
options.C: The seasons themselves become a little shorter each year, so the lunar months can no longer keep pace with them.
options.D: Twelve lunar months total more than 365 days, so the lunar year runs long and the months drift the other way.
